---
title: "Hosea"
---

# Hosea

::: {.book-summary}
## Book Summary Insight

Hosea portrays God's faithful covenant love despite Israel's spiritual unfaithfulness. The book teaches that God's redeeming love pursues His people even after repeated rebellion.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 1

<div class="key-verse">Hosea 1:2</div>

<div class="identifier">Go, take unto thee a wife of whoredoms</div>

### Why This Verse

Symbolic beginning of Hosea's ministry

### Chapter Insight

This chapter introduces Hosea's marriage as a symbol of Israel's unfaithfulness. The key verse demonstrates God's continuing covenant purposes despite His people's rebellion.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 2

<div class="key-verse">Hosea 2:23</div>

<div class="identifier">I will have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy</div>

### Why This Verse

Quoted in Romans and 1 Peter

### Chapter Insight

This chapter portrays God's judgment and future restoration of Israel. The key verse reveals God's desire to draw His people back into loving relationship with Him.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 3

<div class="key-verse">Hosea 3:1</div>

<div class="identifier">Love a woman beloved of her friend</div>

### Why This Verse

Picture of redeeming love

### Chapter Insight

This chapter records Hosea's redemption of his unfaithful wife. The key verse illustrates God's redeeming love toward His wayward people.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 4

<div class="key-verse">Hosea 4:6</div>

<div class="identifier">My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge</div>

### Why This Verse

One of Hosea's most quoted verses

### Chapter Insight

This chapter accuses Israel of lacking knowledge of God. The key verse warns that spiritual destruction results from rejecting God's truth.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 5

<div class="key-verse">Hosea 5:15</div>

<div class="identifier">In their affliction they will seek Me early</div>

### Why This Verse

Repentance theme

### Chapter Insight

This chapter announces judgment upon Israel and Judah. The key verse emphasizes that God disciplines His people to bring them to repentance.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 6

<div class="key-verse">Hosea 6:6</div>

<div class="identifier">I desired mercy, and not sacrifice</div>

### Why This Verse

Quoted by Jesus twice in Matthew

### Chapter Insight

This chapter calls for sincere repentance and covenant faithfulness. The key verse highlights God's desire for mercy and knowledge of Him rather than empty ritual.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 7

<div class="key-verse">Hosea 7:8</div>

<div class="identifier">Ephraim is a cake not turned</div>

### Why This Verse

Memorable image of compromise

### Chapter Insight

This chapter exposes Israel's hypocrisy and political compromises. The key verse illustrates the instability that comes from divided loyalties.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 8

<div class="key-verse">Hosea 8:7</div>

<div class="identifier">They have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind</div>

### Why This Verse

Frequently quoted principle

### Chapter Insight

This chapter warns of the consequences of sowing rebellion. The key verse teaches that people reap the results of their actions.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 9

<div class="key-verse">Hosea 9:17</div>

<div class="identifier">They shall be wanderers among the nations</div>

### Why This Verse

Consequence of rebellion

### Chapter Insight

This chapter announces coming judgment and exile. The key verse emphasizes the consequences of persistent unfaithfulness.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 10

<div class="key-verse">Hosea 10:12</div>

<div class="identifier">Sow to yourselves in righteousness</div>

### Why This Verse

Call to spiritual renewal

### Chapter Insight

This chapter condemns Israel's prosperity without devotion. The key verse calls God's people to seek the Lord and pursue righteousness.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 11

<div class="key-verse">Hosea 11:1</div>

<div class="identifier">Out of Egypt have I called My son</div>

### Why This Verse

Quoted in Matthew regarding Christ

### Chapter Insight

This chapter reveals God's fatherly love for Israel. The key verse expresses God's compassion even toward a rebellious people.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 12

<div class="key-verse">Hosea 12:6</div>

<div class="identifier">Turn thou to thy God</div>

### Why This Verse

Call to covenant faithfulness

### Chapter Insight

This chapter reviews Israel's history and continued need for repentance. The key verse calls for steadfast love, justice, and dependence upon God.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 13

<div class="key-verse">Hosea 13:14</div>

<div class="identifier">O death, I will be thy plagues</div>

### Why This Verse

Quoted in 1 Corinthians 15

### Chapter Insight

This chapter warns of judgment resulting from idolatry. The key verse reminds Israel that God alone is their Savior.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 14

<div class="key-verse">Hosea 14:9</div>

<div class="identifier">Who is wise, and he shall understand these things?</div>

### Why This Verse

Book's concluding wisdom statement

### Chapter Insight

This chapter concludes with a call to repentance and a promise of restoration. The key verse reveals God's willingness to heal and restore those who return to Him.
:::
